genius.notes: As of 2026-10-07, the July 31, 2026 USN terms explicitly identify Noon YBS Issuer Ltd, a British Virgin Islands company, as issuer. USN holders have no entitlement to reserve yield or equity; staking sUSN is a separate position with separate terms and operator. Binding USN redemption is into USDC/USDT or permitted substitute digital assets; no fiat-cash redemption obligation was found, leaving GENIUS applicability unclear. The legal terms provide a standard five-business-day processing period, fees, verification, discretionary delays and gates, whereas the operational mint/redeem page advertises T+0 up to 20% TVL; the legal qualifications are not replaced by that operational description. The Accountable dashboard and its live public data endpoint disclose reserves, liabilities and ongoing proofs; continuous verification is not a monthly independent reserve-attestation report. No public GENIUS approval, official application, state qualification or foreign registration for this exact issuer was located in the reviewed materials and name searches. This bounded negative finding is not a determination of illegality. Treasury describes anticipated GENIUS general effectiveness on January 18, 2027 and the general DASP offer/sale restriction on July 18, 2028; not-yet-restricted remains appropriate on this review date.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: Reviewed on 2026-10-07: no source in the opened federal rulemaking materials, NYDFS directory, issuer terms or exact-name regulator searches names Noon YBS Issuer Ltd as a GENIUS-approved issuer, officially pending applicant, state-qualified issuer or registered foreign issuer. The Federal Reserve issuer framework remains a September 29 NPRM; the September 30 SCRC interim final rule is procedural and states submissions await PRA approval and Treasury notice. This is a bounded public-source negative review, not proof that no private or future filing exists, and not a global claim that every regulator or application database was reviewed.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USN is marketed as a transferable non-yielding dollar-pegged stored-value token, supporting payment design and stable-value expectation. However, July 31, 2026 binding terms promise verified users redemption into Supported Stablecoins, initially USDC and USDT, at USD 1 worth per USN, not payment in national currency or a bank deposit. GENIUS section 2(22)(A)(ii)(I) expressly excludes a digital asset denominated in fixed monetary value from the required redemption consideration; the OCC proposal repeats that distinction. No separate binding fiat-cash redemption obligation was located, so the payment-stablecoin threshold remains unclear rather than presumed solely from the dollar peg.
